name: Emma Wiesner - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directive 2007/2/EC as regards simplification of certain requirements for the establishment of the Infrastructure for Spatial Information in the Union
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to simplify the European Union's rules on sharing maps and other geographic data about the environment, known as the INSPIRE rules. The Commission proposed removing many technical requirements and relying instead on general European Union data laws. Parliament agrees with cutting duplication but wants to keep some safeguards: data should stay findable, comparable and usable across borders, and public bodies should still be able to share it for environmental tasks.

- Parliament keeps open standards for map data and keeps a lighter duty to share data between public bodies.
- It affects national, regional and local public authorities that publish environmental map data.
- Parliament's position now goes to the Council of ministers for negotiation; the text is not final law yet.
